subject.title: memory_search: chokidar file watcher silently stops delivering events, index goes stale

question: Should OpenClaw make memory search periodic sync a default safety net for unconfigured users, or keep it opt-in despite the stale-index watcher failure?
rationale: The remaining fix changes fallback/default behavior, which root AGENTS.md treats as compatibility-sensitive and product-owned even when it mitigates a real bug.

options.title: Accept default fallback
options.body: Land the linked PR direction after repair/review, with `intervalMinutes: 0` preserved as the explicit opt-out and proof for fresh installs and upgrades.

options.title: Keep fallback opt-in
options.body: Leave current defaults unchanged and document `memorySearch.sync.intervalMinutes` as the workaround for users who see watcher drift.

options.title: Close as watcher-rework solved
options.body: Close only if maintainers decide the current native watcher rework sufficiently solves the observable problem without a periodic fallback.

recommendation.title: Accept default fallback
recommendation.body: Land the linked PR direction after repair/review, with `intervalMinutes: 0` preserved as the explicit opt-out and proof for fresh installs and upgrades.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses memory-search behavior, defaults, and compatibility policy, and steipete has the strongest feature-history signal on the memory search surface.
